title: S. Korea actor says 'The Blue Road' helped him break out of acting rut
text:
S. Korea actor says 'The Blue Road' helped him break out of acting rut

Korea actor says 'The Blue Road' helped him break out of acting rut By Lee Minji, Yonhap - Nov 19, 2026 - 12:55 All , World SEOUL - Actor Son Suk-ku, who portrays South Korean detective Kim Seok in the upcoming Netflix original series "The Blue Road," has said the role helped him take on new challenges at a time when he felt stuck in his acting career. Adapted from a 2002 manga of the same name, the series follows Kim, a detective with the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency, as he teams up with Inose (Eita Nagayama) of the Tokyo Metropolitan Police Department to track down a serial killer who leaves cryptic messages. "Personally, I felt as if I had hit a limit as an actor ... like a sprinter who cannot break the 13-second barrier (in the 100 meters)," Son said at a press conference Tuesday for the series held in Seoul. "But (the work) made me feel that I could break through this wall and go over to the next stage." Son credited director Han Jun-hee with encouraging him to experiment, saying their shared willingness to try new things prompted Son to pitch more ideas and to change his voice and appearance for the role, something he had found difficult in the past. Nagayama echoed the view, saying the chemistry between the lead actors and the director and their openness for new changes helped drive the production. "I am an actor who does not feel attracted to pursuing one way of acting, and director Han also seemed to have that kind of attitude," the Japanese actor said, adding, "When I worked with Son, we went with what felt right on set." Against such a backdrop, the actors said working in different languages was not a major hurdle. Actors Jung Jae-young, Choi Sung-eun, Eita Nagayama, Son Suk-ku and Kim Shin-rok (from L to R) pose during a press conference for the upcoming Netflix series "The Blue Road" held in Seoul on Nov. 17, 2026. (Yonhap) Son said rather than being daunted by the fact that Japanese is not his mother tongue, he focused on using Japanese to express his thoughts and approached learning his lines as though he were memorizing a piece of music. Nagayama said his personal connection with Son made working across different languages easier. "When I first met Son, I was nervous because I was also his fan. But I could soon sense that we are the same type of people and instinctively felt that we could overcome the barrier of language and nationality," the actor said. "I was never worried about the human-to-human connection and was truly happy to act with him." For the Japanese actor, whose appearance in "The Blue Road" marks his first major role in a Korean project, taking part in it was also an opportunity to get to know about South Korea and fall in love with the country. "During filming, I went to many cities across the country, including Gwangju, Gunsan and Busan. During breaks, I met a lot of people in small neighborhoods, like grandmothers peeling garlic and people working in local markets, and this really made me fall in love with the people of Korea," the actor said. "I really hope that Korean viewers will love watching the series." The hard-boiled crime series also features veteran actor Jung Jae-young as Seo Hyun-tae, a mysterious figure in Japan's criminal underworld, and Kim Shin-rok as Li Yoon-ok, a Zainichi Korean businesswoman who works with Seo. Directed by Han, known for hit Netflix shows, such as "D.P." and "Weak Hero Class 1," "The Blue Road" is set to premiere Friday.
